source.title: Complete or Sparse: A Tale of Two Identifiabilities

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses monosemantic neurons and reports related synthetic and cross-system results, but it does not test any of the listed claim versions: it does not audit neuron-pole job shares, test held-out neuron explanations, or evaluate attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The experiments measure axis alignment in idealized synthetic data and associations between interpretability scores and cross-system unit correlations. Those results concern neuron interpretability but do not measure the Qwen audit shares or any of the specific behaviors named in V1–V7. The paper's cited examples and prior-work findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is identifiability theory with synthetic validation, plus MIS–MMU cross-system correlations. It discusses monosemantic and grandmother-cell neurons but does not measure any version's quantity. There are no neuron-pole job shares (V1/V2), no reanalysis of InceptionV1's cat/car neuron (V3), and no interpretable-neuron shares across tools or architectures (V4). It builds no attribution graphs (V5) and does no held-out test of explanation or simulation scoring (V6/V7). The weight-decay result (R4–R7) touches V4's 'regularization' wording only in a 5-latent toy network, and its measure is axis alignment (MCC) against known latents, not a share of interpretable neurons. So it is a related construct, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. With capacity m≥n′ the optimal encoder is linear in the latents; with m<n′ it is generically nonlinear. Exact capacity plus non-negativity and an energy constraint gives axis-aligned, grandmother-cell-like neurons. Sparse latents with the spark condition give compressed-sensing structure, so sparse dictionary learning recovers latents, which the authors offer as an explanation of SAE success. Real-data MIS–MMU associations are consistent with cross-system convergence, but the authors caution about the gap to real systems.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops identifiability theory and tests it using synthetic supervised classification, plus MIS–MMU measurements on real model activations; it does not use the neuron-pole auditing or explanation-scoring procedures in the claim sources.
record.method_sensitivity: In the synthetic axis-alignment experiment, outcomes vary with latent DGP, output activation, weight decay, and departures from non-negative latent support. Cross-system associations are reported as weaker for language models than for vision models.

fits_no_version.finding: At exact capacity, a sparse non-negative DGP with ReLU output converges, slowly, to axis-aligned neurons. Linear output or a hyperspherical DGP retains mixed selectivity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In synthetic supervised settings, monosemantic (axis-aligned) units arise only with non-negative latents and outputs plus an energy constraint.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight decay raises the share of seeds reaching MCC≥0.90 from 3/10 (no weight decay) to 10/10 (0.03), with median final MCC rising from 0.878 to 0.987.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy networks, regularization strongly affects whether neurons become axis-aligned.

fits_no_version.finding: Below capacity (m<n′) MLP encoders beat linear ones on KL; at or above capacity both reach near-zero KL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capacity bottlenecks force nonlinear, non-identifiable codes.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-neuron MIS correlates positively with best cross-model matching correlation: in all 12 vision pairs, more weakly in the 3 LMs, and non-significantly in macaque IT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More interpretable units are more likely to have counterparts in other systems.

fits_no_version.finding: Under compressed sensing, unsupervised dictionary learning recovers latents with MCC ≈0.86 at 1-sparse, falling as k grows. Supervised Lasso is near-perfect, while OLS plateaus at R²≈n′/n (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse latents allow SAE-style recovery from polysemantic undercomplete codes.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablations: signed latents collapse MCC (0.770 at flip probability 0.1, 0.049 at 0.5). Log-normal conditionals reduce MCC to 0.668, and entropy SD of 2 nats to 0.662 with a bias-free readout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Axis alignment in toy models depends on non-negative latent support.

record.problems: The principal axis-alignment and capacity experiments use idealized synthetic data and assume global optimality in the theory. Real-data interpretability is proxied by MIS and cross-system matching rather than direct latent labels; the authors caution that their framework has a substantial gap from real systems. Some plot results are described qualitatively in the text rather than with numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-specific result rows were omitted. The paper's supplementary assumption-ablation results are not listed because they do not measure any of the claim versions; the central synthetic axis-alignment and weight-decay outcomes relevant to neuron interpretability are recorded above.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B is not studied; no pole-level shares for one job, two jobs or unknown.
No neuron-job shares in any LLM, dense or MoE, and no scale sweep. Only last-layer MIS in GPT-2 small, Pythia-70m and TinyLlama, used as a proxy for cross-model matching.
No reanalysis of InceptionV1 or of the cat/car neuron, and no test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No interpretable-neuron shares in real vision models across tools or architectures. Weight decay and output non-negativity affect axis alignment only in a synthetic 5-latent toy.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No test of whether explanations from activating examples predict firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses call stands. The paper's closest touchpoint is V4's regularization claim, but it is a toy axis-alignment result, not a share of interpretable neurons in real models. The compressed-sensing results and assumption ablations are unrecorded but bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not audit Qwen3-32B or report proportions of poles with one job, two jobs, or unknown jobs.
It does not estimate comparable neuron-job shares across models or scale, including dense or mixture-of-experts models.
It does not reassess InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or test recursive generalization against superposition.

It studies synthetic capacity and regularization effects on axis alignment, but does not estimate interpretability shares in InceptionV1-sized vision models or test the claimed architecture/tools explanation.
It does not build or evaluate attribution graphs.
It does not test whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict firing on new examples.
It does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.operation_detail: Measured axis alignment using MCC after Hungarian matching between recovered axes and ground-truth latents.

rows.note: This is a synthetic identifiability result, not a count of interpretable neurons in a language model.

rows.subject: synthetic undercomplete encoders
rows.operation_detail: Compared final KL for linear and MLP encoders across encoder dimensions and three latent distributions.
rows.measure: Final KL(p*∥q); the MLP achieves lower KL than the linear encoder at every undercomplete dimension, with the gap closing toward the threshold.
rows.value: MLP has lower final KL at every m<n′ across all three distributions.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± s.e.m. over 10 seeds; numeric values not stated in text.
rows.note: This tests nonlinear identifiability under a synthetic capacity bottleneck, not shares of interpretable neurons.

rows.subject: macaque IT cortex, Tito → Chabo
rows.operation_detail: Measured directional correlation between MIS and MMU across neuronal responses.
rows.note: The authors describe this direction as positive; this is biological-neuron evidence, not an AI-model neuron-job share.
rows.check: r=0.158 with p=0.0986 is not statistically significant against ρ=0. Under the rules a non-significant effect is absent, although the authors call it positive.
